name: Congenital Pulmonary Valvar Stenosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Pulmonary Valve Stenosis

criteria.description: Presence of increased peak systolic gradient across the pulmonary valve > 30 mmHg on echocardiography
Dome-shaped or dysplastic pulmonary valve leaflets visualized on echocardiography
Systolic ejection murmur best heard at the upper left sternal border
Right ventricular hypertrophy on ECG or imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of increased peak systolic gradient > 30 mmHg across pulmonary valve on echocardiography plus characteristic valve morphology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings supported by clinical examination.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; BNP may be elevated in advanced cases
imaging: Echocardiography showing domed pulmonary valve leaflets and increased transvalvular gradient
Chest X-ray showing post-stenotic dilation of pulmonary artery and right ventricular enlargement
genetic: Usually sporadic; occasionally associated with Noonan syndrome and other genetic syndromes
other: Cardiac catheterization may confirm gradient and anatomy if noninvasive imaging inconclusive

distinguishingFeatures: Right ventricular outflow tract obstruction with cyanosis
Complete absence of pulmonary valve opening
Dependence on ductus arteriosus for pulmonary blood flow

references: Maron BJ, et al. Pulmonary Valve Stenosis. In: Braunwald's Heart Disease, 12th Edition. 2021.
Orphanet: Congenital Pulmonary Valvar Stenosis. ORPHA:3189.
American Heart Association Guidelines for the Management of Congenital Heart Disease, 2020.
